description:
A calmer desktop. Everything within reach.

Give every project a place. PecoFence organizes your Windows 11 and 10 desktop into fences: glass panels that keep your files close and give your wallpaper room to breathe.

FIND IT AS YOU TYPE
Press Ctrl + Alt + Space to bring your fences above the current app, then just type: matching files and folders show up at once, Chinese names by pinyin or initials included. Enter opens one, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 picks it, and Esc takes you back to work. Turn on the free Everything search and the whole computer is searched as well. Choose Press Ctrl twice as the shortcut, and a quick double press of Ctrl opens your fences with the search box ready.

THE RIGHT FOLDER IN EVERY OPEN AND SAVE DIALOG
In an Open or Save As dialog, switch to File Explorer and back, and the dialog jumps to the folder Explorer shows. Ctrl+G or a click on a folder fence does it too, and Enter on a search result hands that file straight to the dialog. It starts off: the first time it could help, PecoFence offers to turn it on, and Settings shows how it works.

LET YOUR AI SET IT UP
PecoFence includes pecofence-cli. Tell a coding agent such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor what you want in your own words: it reads your current setup and applies the changes, from new fences and sorting rules to icon sizes, colors and themes. Snapshots and configuration export keep a copy of a setup you like.

LESS TIME SORTING
Set rules for file types, names, age or size. New desktop files appear in the right fence automatically. Automatic sorting leaves their locations on disk unchanged.

SMALL TOOLS WHEN YOU WANT THEM
Add notes with to-dos, a clock with the date, or a script fence that shows what your own script prints, such as the weather; its rows can open a link or tick a to-do when you click them. Each tool stays off until you turn it on under Tools in Settings.

A SPACE FOR EVERY PROJECT
Combine related fences into tabs. Switch in a click, or drag a tab out into its own fence. Keep a live folder on the desktop and browse its subfolders in place.

MAKE ROOM FOR FOCUS
Double-click empty desktop space to hide your fences and again to bring them back. Roll a fence up to its title bar and hover to expand it.

GLASS THAT FITS YOUR DESKTOP
Choose Fluent or Liquid Glass, light or dark, then adjust each fence's color and opacity. Save your layout with snapshots and backups.

LIGHT ON YOUR PC
PecoFence is a native application that uses about 2 to 5 MB of memory at rest, as shown in Task Manager. The settings window loads only when you open it.

Free and open source under Apache 2.0. No app account required. Eleven built-in display languages, available offline. Designed for Windows 10 22H2 / Windows 11 x64.

PecoFence uses real files: file operations you initiate, including moves, renames and deletions, affect files on disk. Your normal Windows desktop icons return when the app exits.

releaseNotes: What's new in this update: the search in Peek at all fences now lists its matches with their icons and fences and finds Chinese names by pinyin; the switch Peek search also finds files on the whole computer (Everything) adds files from the whole computer, and Peek's shortcut can be Press Ctrl twice. New Jump in file dialogs: an Open or Save dialog jumps to the folder of the File Explorer window you come back from, and Ctrl+G jumps there at any time; the first time it could help, PecoFence offers to turn it on, and Settings shows how it works. Settings has a new Tools page with small tools in fences: Notes and to-dos (a line that starts with [ ] becomes a to-do that a click ticks), Clock and date, and Script fence, which shows what a script of yours prints, with rows that can be clicked (Add example… offers four ready scripts). The mouse's back and forward buttons work in a fence that shows a folder. Find a setting (Ctrl+F) at the top left of Settings finds any setting. The first start shows a few tips, and an update shows what is new. Fixes: on Windows 10, Peek at all fences no longer closes right after it opens; a shortcut's menu lists Open file location only once; How rolled-up fences expand and Windows desktop icons are each one list.
